title: The King and the Beard

full_text:
King Krishnadevaraya was intensely proud of his full, majestic, jet-black imperial beard, which he groomed daily with scented oils and comb.
One morning, the royal barber, an elderly, loyal craftsman named Ramdas whose hands had begun to tremble with age, accidentally slipped with his sharp steel shears.
*SNIP!*
A massive chunk of the King's beard on the left cheek was sliced away completely, leaving an awkward, bare patch!

The King looked into his silver hand mirror and let out a roar of thunderous fury:
'Incompetent fool! Thou hast mutilated the Emperor's royal countenance!
Guards! Take this wretch to the courtyard and have his hands bound for banishment!'

Poor Ramdas fell to the marble floor, trembling, weeping, clutching the King's feet in despair.
Tenali Raman, who was entering the chamber for morning consultation, took in the scene at a glance.

Tenali did not argue with the King or make excuses for the barber.
Instead, he walked up to King Krishnadevaraya, looked intently at the King's newly shortened beard, and clapped his hands in theatrical admiration:
'Jahanpanah! Congratulations! What a magnificent, youthful transformation!
I had heard that the emperors of Persia and Rome trim their beards closely to reveal the chiseled jawlines of warrior-heroes, but I never dreamed our own Emperor would adopt this heroic fashion!'

The King paused, his hand halfway to his scabbard, looking confused:
'Youthful transformation? Heroic fashion?'

Tenali continued with enthusiastic praise:
'Indeed, Maharaj! For ten years, your full beard made you look like a venerable, sixty-year-old grandfather sage!
Now, with your jawline exposed by this modern trim, you look barely twenty-five years old—a dashing, invincible general ready to lead cavalry charges into battle!
Your enemies will tremble at the sight of your fierce, youthful vigor!
In fact, Maharaj, order the barber to trim the right side to match immediately, so the entire court may celebrate your youthful majesty!'

The King looked back into the silver mirror.
He tilted his head, imagined himself as a dashing twenty-five-year-old warrior, and a broad smile broke across his face.
The King chuckled, then burst into hearty laughter:
'Ha-ha! Tenali, thou art right! A heavy beard makes a man look old before his time!'

The King turned to the trembling barber:
'Ramdas, rise! Trim the other side to match, and take this gold coin for thy service, but keep thy hands steady henceforth!'

Ramdas wept tears of gratitude, kissing Tenali’s feet.
Tenali smiled, having turned an execution into a celebration through the sovereign magic of tactful wit.
moral: A skillful word of witty reassurance can turn sudden anger into pleasant laughter and pardon.
